chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God have Mercy upon him - quoted his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamedany who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Davood ibn Farqad, on the authority of either Abi Ja’far or Aba Abdullah (peace be upon them), who said:
Three groups of people are not pure: Those whose right eye is blind; those whose pupils are like the stone on a ring, and those who are born as Sindi.

key_terms.الْفَصِّ: the stone on a ring (specifically referring to the pupil)

ai.seo_question: What are the three conditions that make a person not pure according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal, this hadith identifies three specific physical or geographical markers—right-eye blindness, a distinctive eye condition resembling a 'fuss' (ring stone), and birth in Sindh—that historically rendered a person 'not pure' (la yanjubu) for certain ritual or social purposes. While often interpreted as physical defects or regional origins affecting ritual status in early Shia jurisprudence, scholars note these conditions may also signify specific lineages or traits relevant to the context of purity laws. This classification highlights the nuanced approach of the Imams in distinguishing between inherent physical states and ritual eligibility.
